And what he meant by his saying by My eyes is in My sight and love by will. And His statement, When your sister walked and said, ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?’ God Almighty says: When your sister walked, she followed you until she found you, then someone came asking for wet nurses for you, and she said, Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him? And what I mentioned after His statement, When your sister walked, was omitted from the speech, as the indication of the speech was sufficient for it. Moses' sister said that to them because: Musa bin Harun narrated: Amr narrated: Asbat narrated: As-Suddi said: When his mother threw him into the river, She said to his sister, ‘Follow him.’ (al-Qasas 28:11) When Pharaoh’s family picked him up and wanted wet nurses for him, he did not take any of the women. The women began to ask for them to stay with Pharaoh to nurse him, but he refused. His sister said: Shall I direct you to a family who will take care of him for you and who will be sincere to him? (al-Qasas 28:2)? So they took her and said: Rather, I know this boy, so direct us to his family. She said: I do not know him, but I only said that they are sincere to the king. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: She said: meaning the mother of Moses to his sister: Take him away and see what they will do with him. So she went out in that regard, and she saw him from a distance while they did not perceive. (al-Qasas 28:11), and he needed to be breastfed and sought the breast, and they gathered wet nurses for him when God bestowed their love upon him, so no woman would be brought to him and he would accept her breast, which would make them weary, and one wet nurse after another would be brought to him, but he would not accept anything from them. So his sister said to them when she saw how much they loved him and how keen they were on him, Shall I direct you to a household who will take him under their care and be sincere to him? (al-Qasas 28:12), meaning because of his status with you and your keenness to please the king. What he meant by his statement, Shall I direct you to someone who will take him under their care? “Shall I direct you to someone who will take him under his care and protect him, breastfeed him, and raise him?” It was said that the meaning of And Zachariah took her under his care (Al Imran 3:37) is to take her under his care. And His statement, And We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve, God Almighty says: So We returned you to your mother after you had become in the hands of Pharaoh’s people, so that her eye might be comforted by your safety and your escape from being killed and drowned in the sea, and so that she would not grieve over you out of fear that Pharaoh would kill you. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Moses’ sister said to them what she said, they said: Bring it. So his mother came and told her, so she went with her until she came to them, and they gave him to her. When she placed him in her lap, he took her breast, and they were pleased with that from him, and God returned him to his mother so that her eyes would be comforted and she would not be sad. So God’s kindness to her and to him reached the point that He returned her son to her and showed her kindness, benefiting Pharaoh and his family with the security from the killing that was feared for others, so it was as if they were from the family of Pharaoh in security and comfort, so he was on Pharaoh’s bed and couch. And His saying, And you killed a soul, means, may His praise be glorified, that the Copt killed him when the Israelite called out to him for help against him, so Moses struck him. And His saying, And We saved you from the distress, means, may His praise be glorified, that We saved you from your distress by your killing the soul that you killed, when they wanted to kill you with it, so We delivered you from them, until you fled to the people of Madyan, and they did not succeed in killing you or your fuel. His killing of him was mentioned as a mistake, as: Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Moses killed the one who was killed from the family of Pharaoh by mistake, so God said to him: ‘And you killed a soul, but We saved you from distress and tested you with trials.’” Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida and Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So We saved you from distress he said: from killing a soul. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So We saved you from the distress means the soul that was killed. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying, And We tested you with trials. Some of them said: We tested you with a trial and examined you with a test. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We tested you with trials, meaning: We tested you with a test. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We tested you with trials, he said: You were afflicted with a trial. Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid Al-Amili told me: Yazid bin Harun told us: Asbagh bin Zaid Al-Juhani told us: Al-Qasim bin Ayoub told me: Saeed bin Jubair told me: I asked Abdullah bin Abbas about the words of God to Moses: And We have tried you with trials. I asked him: What are the trials? He said to me: Start the day again, O Ibn Jubair, for they have a long story. He said: When morning came, I went to Ibn Abbas to fulfill his promise to me. Ibn Abbas said: Pharaoh and his companions were discussing what God had promised Abraham, that He would make prophets and kings among his descendants. Some of them said: The Children of Israel are waiting for that and they do not doubt it, and they thought that he was Joseph, son of Jacob. But when he died, they said: This is not how God promised Abraham. Pharaoh said: What do you think? He said: So they consulted among themselves and agreed that he would send men with knives to go around among the Children of Israel, and they would not find a male child without slaughtering him. When they saw that the adults of the Children of Israel were dying at their appointed times, and the young were being slaughtered, they said: You are about to annihilate the Children of Israel, and you will be at the point where you will be able to do the work and service that they used to do for you. So kill every male child one year, and their children will decrease, and leave a year in which you will not kill any of them, and the young will grow up in place of those who die from the adults, for they will not increase in number because of those whom you are ashamed of, and you will fear their increasing number with you, and they will not decrease in number because of those whom you kill. So they agreed on that, and Moses’ mother became pregnant with Aaron in the following year in which boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely, until the following year she became pregnant with Moses, and worry and sadness fell into her heart, and that is from the trials, O Ibn Jubayr, because of what entered upon him in his mother’s womb, which was intended for him. So God revealed to her: “And do not fear, nor grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers.” (al-Qasas 28:7), and He commanded her when she gave birth to him to put him in a chest and then throw him into the sea. So when she gave birth to him, she did what she was commanded to do, until her son disappeared from her, Satan came to her, and she said to herself: What have I done with my son? If he were slaughtered near me and I hid him and shrouded him, it would be dearer to me than to throw him with my hand to the whales and beasts of the sea. So the water carried him away until it reached him at the watering place of the female servants of Pharaoh’s family. They saw him and seized him, and they intended to open the door, but some of them said to one another: There is money in this, and if we open it, Pharaoh’s wife will not believe us in what we found in it. So they carried him as he was, without moving a thing of it, until they gave him to her. When she opened it, she saw the boy in it, and she bestowed upon him a love from her that she had never bestowed upon anyone else. And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty. (al-Qasas 28:7) A] From everything except the mention of Moses, so when the slaughterers heard of his command, they came to Pharaoh’s wife with their knives, intending to slaughter him, and that is from the trials, O Ibn Jubayr, so she said to the slaughterers: Go away from me, for this one will not increase the number of the Children of Israel, so I will go to Pharaoh and ask him for him, for if he gives him to me, you will have done well and been beautiful, and if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you, so when she brought him to Pharaoh, she said: A comfort of the eye for me and for you (al-Qasas 28:19) Pharaoh said: He will be for you, but as for me, I have no need of him, so he said: By the One by whom he swears, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be a comfort of the eye as she acknowledged him, God would have guided him through him as He guided his wife through him, but God forbade him that, so she sent to those around her from every female who had milk, to choose a wet nurse for him, so whenever one of them took him to nurse him, he would not accept her breast, until Pharaoh’s wife feared that he would refuse milk and die, so that saddened her, So she ordered him to go out to the market where the people were gathered, hoping to find a wet nurse for him who would take him from her, but no one accepted. Then the mother of Moses came in the morning and said to his sister: “Take him and look for him. Do you hear any mention of him? Is my son alive, or have the sea creatures and whales eaten him and forgotten what God had promised her?” Then his sister saw him from afar while they did not notice, and she said with joy when the wet nurses were exhausted: I will guide you to a family who will take care of him for you and will be sincere to him. So they took her and said: How do you know that they gave him sincere advice? Do they know him? Until they doubted that, and that is from the temptations, O Ibn Jubayr, so she said: Their advice to him and their compassion for him, their desire to wet the king’s womb, and the hope of his benefit, so they left her, so she went to her mother and told her the report, so she came, and when she placed him in her lap, he climbed onto her breast until his sides were filled, so the good report went to Pharaoh’s wife to give her the good report that we have found a wet nurse for your son, so she sent to her, and she was brought with him, and when she saw what was being done to her, she said: Stay with me until you nurse this son of mine, for I have never loved anything like him, he said: So she said: I cannot leave my house and my children, and they will be lost, so if you are content to give him to me, so I can take him to my house and he will be with me, and I will not spare him any good, I will do it, but if not, then I will not leave my house and my children, and Moses’ mother remembered what God had promised her, so she was distressed with Pharaoh’s wife and was certain that God, Blessed and Exalted be He, will fulfill His promise, so she returned with her son to her house that same day, So God made him grow well and preserved him for what He had decreed for him. The Children of Israel, while they were gathered in the area of the city, continued to protect themselves through him from the oppression and forced labor that was upon them. When he grew up, Pharaoh’s wife said to Moses’ mother: Visit my son with me. She promised her one day that she would visit him with him. She said to her confidants, her wet nurses, and her servants: “Let not one of you remain without receiving my son with a gift and honor so that he may see that. I am sending a trustworthy woman who will record everything that every person among you does.” So gifts, honor, and presents continued to greet him from the time he left his mother’s house until he entered upon Pharaoh’s wife. When he entered upon her, she bestowed honor upon him and was happy with him. She was pleased with what she saw of the good effect she had on him. She said: Take him to Pharaoh, so that he may bestow honor upon him and honor him. When they entered upon him, she placed him in his lap. Moses took hold of Pharaoh’s beard until he stretched it out. Then one of God’s enemies said: Do you not see what God promised Abraham, that He will overthrow you and overcome you? So he sent for the slaughterers to slaughter him. This was from O Ibn Jubayr, after every trial that I have been afflicted with and that I have been wanted for, then Pharaoh’s wife came running to Pharaoh and said: What do you think of this boy whom you have given me? He said: Don’t you see that he claims that he will defeat me and overcome me. She said: Make a matter between me and you in which you will know the truth. Bring two live coals and two pearls and bring them near to him. If he grabs the pearls and avoids the live coals, you will know that he is sane. But if he reaches for the live coals and does not want the pearls, then know that no one would prefer the live coals to the pearls while he is sane. So they brought them near to him and he reached for the live coals, but they took them away from him for fear that they would burn his hand. The woman said: Don’t you see? So God turned him away from him after what he had intended to do, and God accomplished His purpose regarding him. When he reached his full maturity and was a man, no one from the family of Pharaoh would get rid of any of the children of Israel with him by oppression or forced labor, until they refused to do so. While he was walking one day in the direction of the city, he saw two men fighting, one of them from the children of Israel and the other from the family of Pharaoh. The Israelite called for help from him against the Pharaoh, and Moses became angry and his anger became intense, because he attacked him while he knew the status of Moses among the children of Israel and his protection of them, and the people did not know except that it was from the breastfeeding of other than Moses’ mother, unless God informed Moses of that which no one else knew of. So Moses struck the Pharaoh and killed him, and no one saw them except God and the Israelite. Moses said when he killed the man: “This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy.” (al-Qasas 28:15) Then he said: My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me. So He forgave him. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” (al-Qasas 28:16) So he became in the city, fearful and watching. (al-Qasas 28:18) The report, so he came to Pharaoh, Then it was said to him: The Children of Israel have killed a man from the family of Pharaoh, so take our right for us and do not give them permission to do so. He said: Find me his killer and someone to testify against him, because it is not right to judge without evidence or proof. So they asked him for that, and while they were wandering around they could not find proof. Then Moses passed by the next day and saw that Israelite fighting a Pharaoh. The Israelite sought help from him against the Pharaoh, and he came across Moses regretting what he had done the day before and hating what he had seen. Moses became angry and stretched out his hand wanting to strike the Pharaoh. Then he said to the Israelite for what he had done yesterday and today: Indeed, you are a clear transgressor (al-Qasas 28:18). The Israelite looked at Moses after what he had said, and he was as angry as he was for the matter in which he had killed the Pharaoh. He feared that after he had said to him: Indeed, you are a clear transgressor (al-Qasas 28:18) he had meant it and had not meant it, but rather he meant the Pharaoh. The Israelite was afraid and blocked the Pharaoh and said: O Moses, do you want to kill me as you killed a person? “Yesterday” (al-Qasas 28:19) He only said that out of fear that Moses wanted to kill him, so they left him. The Pharaoh went to his people and told them what he had heard from the Israelite when he said: Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? So Pharaoh sent the slaughterers, and Moses took the main road, and they sought him without fearing that they would miss him. A man from the party of Moses came from the farthest part of the city, and he took a short path until he reached Moses before them, and he told him the report. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, trials, he said: The affliction of his being thrown into the chest, then into the sea, then the Pharaoh’s family picking him up, then his coming out afraid. Muhammad ibn Amr said, and Abu Asim said: Afraid, or hungry. Abu Asim was uncertain. Al-Harith said: Afraid, watching, but he was not uncertain. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, and he said: fearful and watching, and he did not doubt. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We tested you with trials, meaning: We afflicted you with a trial. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We tested you with trials, that it is a trial following a trial. Others said: The meaning of this is: We have saved you. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And We tested you with tests. We purified you with purity. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Ya`la Ibn Muslim, he said: I heard Sa`id Ibn Jubayr interpreting this word And We have tried you with trials. He said: We have purified you with purity. Abu Jaafar said: We have previously explained in this book of ours the meaning of the trial, that it is a test and trial, with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And his saying, So you remained among the people of Madyan for years. Some of what was complete in this statement has been omitted, as the indication of what was mentioned is sufficient for what was omitted. The meaning of the statement is: And We tested you with trials, so you went out in fear to the people of Madyan, and you remained among them for years. And His saying, Then you came at the appointed time, O Moses, God Almighty says: Then you came at the time when we wanted to send you as a messenger to Pharaoh and for the appointed time. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then you came at a certain time, O Moses, meaning: You came to a certain time, O Moses. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Mujahid, he said: According to a certain amount, O Moses. He said: An appointment. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: On an appointment. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, according to a certain measure, O Moses, he said: the measure of the message and prophethood. The Arabs say: So-and-so came according to a certain measure: if he came to the time when he was needed, and from this is the saying of the poet: He attained the caliphate or it was a destiny for him as his Lord gave Moses according to destiny.
20:41: God Almighty says: And I chose you for Myself. I bestowed these blessings upon you, O Moses, and bestowed these favors upon you, as My choosing you, and selecting you for My message and to convey My message, and to carry out My commands and prohibitions.
20:42: Go, you and your brother Aaron with My signs meaning: with My evidence and arguments, go to Pharaoh with them, for he has rebelled in his misguidance and error, so convey to him My messages first. Then be weak in remembering Me, meaning: and do not be weak in remembering Me in what I have commanded you and forbidden you, for remembering Me strengthens your resolve and makes your feet firm, because if you remember Me, you will remember from Me many blessings upon you, and countless favors. It is said from this: So-and-so was weak in this matter, and about this matter: if he was weak, and he was weak and feeble, as Al-Ajjaj said: He has not been weak since God forgave him for his past and future sins. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And do not be slow, meaning: Do not delay. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And do not slacken in remembering Me, meaning: Do not be weak in remembering Me. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And do not slacken in remembering Me, he said: Do not become weak. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Tanya means weakness. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not slacken in remembering Me, meaning: Do not be weak in remembering Me. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And do not slacken in remembering Me, he said: Do not weaken. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And do not slacken in remembering Me, meaning: Do not become weak. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And do not slacken in remembering Me, he said: The one who is absent-minded is the one who is negligent and excessive. That is the one who is absent-minded.
20:43: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.
20:44: God Almighty says to Moses and Aaron: So speak to Pharaoh with gentle speech. He mentioned that the gentle speech that God commanded them to say to him was to call him by his nickname. Jaafar Ibn Bint Ishaq Ibn Yusuf Al-Azraq told me: Saeed Ibn Muhammad Al-Thaqafi told us: Ali Ibn Salih told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then speak to him with gentle speech. He said: His nickname. His saying, Perhaps he will remember or fear. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his saying, Perhaps in this place. Some of them said that its meaning here is a question, as if they directed the meaning of the speech to: So speak to him with gentle speech, and see if he will remember and reconsider or fear God, so that he will be deterred from his transgression. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Perhaps he will remember or fear, he said: Does he remember or fear? Others said: The meaning of perhaps here is so that. They directed the meaning of the speech to Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. So call him and admonish him so that he may remember or fear, just as someone says: Do your work so that you may receive your reward, meaning: so that you may receive your reward. And finish your work so that we may eat lunch,” meaning: so that we may eat lunch, or so that we may eat lunch. Both of these sayings have a good aspect and a correct approach.
20:45: And His saying, They said, 'Our Lord, indeed we fear that he will overstep his bounds upon us.' God Almighty says: Moses and Aaron said: Our Lord, indeed we fear that Pharaoh, if we call him to what you have commanded us to call him to, will hasten the punishment upon us. It is from their saying: A matter overstepped from me to so-and-so, if it preceded it from him to him. And from it: He overstepped the bounds, meaning the one who hastens ahead of them to the water or the house, as the rajaz poet said: The foreigner has been too aggressive towards us and hastened As for excess: it is extravagance, excess, and transgression. It is said: you exaggerated in your speech: if you were excessive in it and transgressed. As for negligence: it is procrastination. It is said: I was negligent in this matter until it passed, meaning he was procrastinating in it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, that he should be excessive towards us, he said: a punishment from him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, we fear that he will be excessive towards us or that he will transgress, he said: We fear that he will be hasty towards us when we convey your words or your command to him, he will be excessive and hasty. And he recited, Do not fear, indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing.
20:46: God Almighty says: God said to Moses and Aaron, Do not fear Pharaoh, I am with you, I will help you against him, and I will see you, I will hear what is going on between you and him, so I will make you understand what you are discussing with him, and I will see what you do and what he does, nothing of that is hidden from me.
20:47: Then go to him and say to him, We are messengers of your Lord. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, He said, ‘Do not fear, for I am with you, I hear and see.’ What he is talking to you about, so he revealed to you and you responded to him. And His statement, So go to him and say, ‘Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord.’ We have been sent to you commanding you to send the Children of Israel with us, so send them with us and do not punish them with the evil deeds that you charge them with. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord, meaning that He has sent us with that, if you do not believe us in what we say to you, we will show it to you. “And peace be upon him who follows the guidance.” He says: And peace be upon him who follows the guidance of God, and this is His explanation. It is said: Peace be upon him who follows the guidance, and to him who follows, with the same meaning.
20:48: God Almighty says to His Messenger Moses and Aaron: Say to Pharaoh, “Indeed, your Lord has revealed to us that His punishment, which has no end and no cessation, will be upon whoever denies what we call him to of the Oneness of God and obedience to Him, and responding to His Messengers.” And he turned away, meaning: and turned away, turning away from what we brought him of the truth. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, The punishment is upon he who denied and turned away, he denied the Book of God and turned away from obeying God.
20:49: And his saying, He said, 'Who is your Lord, O Moses?' in this statement is omitted. He omitted mentioning it because what was mentioned about it was sufficient, which is his saying, So they went to him, and said to him what their Lord had commanded them to do and conveyed to him His message. Then Pharaoh said to them, Who is your Lord, O Moses? So he addressed Moses alone by saying, O Moses, and the speech had been directed before that to Moses and his brother. And he did that in this way because the response is only from one person even if the address is to the group and not to everyone, and that is similar to his saying, They forgot their fish (al-Kahf 18:61) and the one who carried the fish was one, and he was Moses' young man, as indicated by his saying, But I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan (al-Kahf 18:63).
20:50: And His statement, He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave each thing its nature and then guided it.' God Almighty says: Moses said to him in response: Our Lord is He who gave each thing its nature, meaning: the likeness of its creation in form and appearance, like the males of the children of Adam, He gave them the likeness of their creation of females as mates, and like the males of the animals, He gave them the likeness of their creation, and in their form and appearance of females as mates, so He did not give man something other than His creation, so He would mate him with females of the animals, nor did the animals with females of mankind, then He guided them to the source from which offspring and growth come, and to all its benefits of food and drink, and other than that. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He gave each thing its nature and then guided it, meaning: He created a wife for each thing, then guided it to its place of marriage, food, drink, dwelling, and birth. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided it. He said: He gave each creature its form and then guided it to marriage. Others said: The meaning of his saying, Then He guided is that He guided them to harmony, meeting, and marriage. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Who gave each thing its form and nature, then guided it, means: He guided some of them to others, brought their hearts together and guided them to marriage, that they should marry each other. Others said: The meaning of this is: He gave everything its image, which is the creation with which He created it, then He guided it to what is suitable for it in terms of deception for food and livelihood. Who said that? Abu Kuraib and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, He gave each thing its nature and then guided it, he said: He gave each thing its form and then guided each thing to its livelihood. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, He gave each thing its nature and then guided it, he said: He created every creature, then guided it to that which is good for it, and taught it that. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and nature and then guided it, he said: He created each creature and then guided it to that which is good for it and taught it that, and He did not make people like the creation of animals, nor did He create animals like the creation of people, but He created each thing and determined it with a determination. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid: He gave each thing its nature and then guided it. He said: He guided it to its means and livelihood. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He gave everything what is good for it, then guided it to it. Who said that? Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He gave each thing its creation, he said: He gave each thing what would be good for it. Then He guided it to it. Abu Ja`far said: We have chosen the statement that we have chosen in interpreting that, because He, the Most High, has informed us that He gave everything He created, and He does not give the giver Himself, rather He gives what is other than Him, because the gift requires the giver to be given and the gift, and the gift cannot be the given, and if it is not Him, but is other than Him, and the image of every creation is some of its parts, it is known that if it is said: He gave man His image, it means that He gave him some of the meanings that he has with others and he is called a human being, so it is as if the one who said it said: He gave every creation itself, and that is not if the speech is directed to it with the known meanings of the gift, even if the speech may bear it. If that is the case, then the most correct of its meanings is that it is directed to everything that his Lord gave him like His creation, so He married him to it, then guided him to what we have explained, then He left out mentioning an example, and it was said: He gave everything its creation, just as it is said: Abdullah is like a lion, then an example is deleted, so one says Abdullah is the lion.
20:51: God Almighty says: Pharaoh said to Moses, when Moses described his Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, with what He described Him with of great authority, and the abundance of blessings and favors upon His creation: What is the matter with the nations that came before us that they did not acknowledge what you say, and did not believe in what you call for, and did not devote worship to Him, but rather worshipped gods and idols instead of Him, if the matter is as you describe, that all things are His creation, and that they change in His blessings, and act in His favors?
20:52: Then Moses answered him and said: The knowledge of these nations that passed before us, regarding what they did, is with my Lord in a Book: meaning in the Mother of the Book. I have no knowledge of their affair, and what was the reason for the misguidance of those of them who went astray and departed from the religion of God. My Lord does not err means: My Lord does not err in His management and actions. If He punished those generations immediately and hastened their destruction, then what He did was right. But if He delayed their punishment until the Day of Resurrection, then what He did was right. He knows best what He does. My Lord does not err, nor does He forget, so He does not abandon what He did out of wisdom and rightness. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, “In a Book. My Lord does not err, nor does He forget,” he says: My Lord does not make mistakes, nor does He forget. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, What about the former generations? He said, What about the former generations? He said, What about the former generations? So the Prophet of God entrusted them with a trustee and said, Their knowledge is with my Lord.... the verse. He said, That is, their ages and their terms. Others said: The meaning of his saying, My Lord does not err, nor does He forget, is one. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, My Lord does not err, nor does He forget, he said: They are one thing. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The Arabs say: So-and-so lost his home if he missed it, he lost it without an alif. And it is the same for everything that is fixed and does not move, but its destination is lost, then they say: he lost it. But if something that moves on its own is lost from it, such as an animal, a camel, or something similar to that of an animal that escapes from it and goes away, then they say: So-and-so lost his camel, sheep, or camel, he lost it with an alif. We have already explained the meaning of forgetfulness in what has passed before, so there is no need to repeat it.
20:53: The people of interpretation differed in reading His statement a cradle. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read it as He who made the earth a cradle for you, with a kasra on the mim of mahad and adding an alif after the ha, and this is what they did throughout the Qur'an. Some of those who chose to read it this way claimed that they chose it because mahad is the name of a place, and mahd is the verb. He said: It is like fursh and bedding. The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as mahd meaning: He who made the earth a cradle for you. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two widely used readings in the readings of the regions and are well-known. So whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct in it. And His saying, And He has made paths for you therein, means: And He has made paths for you on the earth. The ha in His saying therein is from the mention of the earth. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He has made paths for you therein: meaning roads. And His statement, And He sent down water from the sky, means: And He sent down rain from the sky, and We brought forth thereby pairs of diverse plants. This is report from God, the Most High, about His favor upon His creation with what happens to them of the rain that He sends down from His sky to His earth, after His report of Moses’ answer to Pharaoh about what he asked him about and his praise of his Lord as He deserves, He, the Most High, says: So We brought forth, O people, with what We send down from the sky of water, pairs, meaning colors of diverse plants, meaning different in tastes, scents, and appearance. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, from various plants, meaning: different.
20:54: God Almighty says: Eat, O people, of the good things We have produced for you by the rain which We have sent down from the sky to the earth, of its fruits and its food, and what is of your sustenance and nourishment, and pasture from it what is provision for your livestock and their sustenance your livestock. Indeed in that are signs. He says: Indeed in what is described in this verse of the power of your Lord and the greatness of His authority are signs: meaning indications and signs that indicate the oneness of your Lord, and that you have no god other than Him. For those of understanding meaning: the people of wisdom and intellect. And understanding is the plural of prohibition, just as kashi is the plural of kashiyyah. Abu Jaafar said: Al-Kashi is a fat that is in the belly of the monitor lizard, similar to the navel. God Almighty mentioned that these are signs for those of understanding, because they are the people of contemplation and consideration, and the people of deliberation and admonition.
20:55: God Almighty says: From the earth We created you, O mankind, and We made you speaking bodies. And into it We will return you. He says: And into the earth We will return you after your death, and We will make you dust, just as you were before We created you, perfect human beings. And from it We will extract you. He says: And from the earth We will extract you just as you were alive before your death, and We will create you from it, just as We created you the first time... And His saying another time means: another time. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And from it We will bring you out another time, meaning: another time. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, another time, he said: another time, the other creation. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the statement then is: We brought you out of the earth, and you were nothing, a perfect creation, and We will bring you out of it after your death once again, just as We brought you out of it the first time.
20:56: God Almighty says: And We showed Pharaoh Our signs, meaning Our evidence and proofs of the truth of what We sent Our messengers Moses and Aaron to him with, all of them. But he denied and refused to accept from Moses and Aaron what they brought from their Lord of the truth, out of arrogance and defiance.
20:57: God Almighty says: When We showed him all Our signs, Pharaoh said to Our Messenger Moses: Have you come to us, O Moses, to drive us out of our homes and houses with this magic that you have brought us?
20:58: Then we will bring you magic like it, so make an appointment between us and you We will not go beyond it, so that we will bring magic like the one you brought, and we will see which of us will defeat the other, we will not break that appointment We and you are in a place of justice He says: in a place of justice between us and you and a half. The readers differed in their reading of this. The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as makān sawa with a kasra on the sīn, and the majority of the readers of Kufa read it as makān sawa with a damma on the sīn. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that they are two dialects, I mean the kasra and damma of the seen in sawa, which are well-known among the Arabs. Scholars of the reciters have recited each of them, and their meanings are in agreement. So whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. And the Arabs have a dialect in this regard, if it means justice and fairness, that is a more well-known kasra and damma, which is the fatha, as God, the Most High, said: Come to a word that is just between us and you (Al Imran 3:64). And if the seen is opened, it is extended, and if it is broken or damma, it is shortened, as the poet said: Our father had settled in a town between Qais Qais Ailan and Al-Fazar. Similar to these names are: Ṭawā folded,...Thāna thana, ʿAdā passive, and ʿAdā passive. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a place that is equal, he said: fair between them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: A just place: meaning, just between us and you. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, a place equal to he said: halfway between us and you. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement, So make between us and you an appointment which neither we nor you will fail to meet, at a place equal to, he said: He says: Justice. Ibn Zayd used to say about that what Yunus told me. He said: Ibn Wahb told us. He said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, a level place, he said: A level place where people can see what is in it, where there is no direction or anything, so that some of it is hidden from some of it, visible and visible.
20:59: God Almighty says: Moses said to Pharaoh, when he asked him to set a time for a meeting between them: Your meeting time is the day of adornment, meaning a day of celebration that they had, or a market in which they adorned themselves. And that the people be gathered, meaning that the people be driven from every direction and place, at noon. That is the time between me and you for a meeting. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He said, ‘Your appointment is the Day of Adornment, and that the people will be gathered at noon.’ It is a day of adornment, on which the people will gather and for which the people will be gathered. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, “He said: Your appointment is on the Day of Adornment.” He said: A day of adornment for them, and a day of celebration for them. And that the people will be gathered at noon, to a celebration for them. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqoub told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed: The day of adornment. He said: The day of the market. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The Day of Adornment is their appointment. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Musa said: Your appointment is on the day of adornment and when the people will be gathered at noon. That is a day of celebration for them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “He said: Your appointment is the day of adornment,” a day of celebration that they had. And His statement, And that the people will be gathered at noon, they will gather for that appointment that they were promised. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He said, ‘Your appointment is the day of adornment.’ He said: The day of Eid, the day when people are free from work, and they witness, attend, and see. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: “He said: Your appointment is on the day of adornment,” a day of celebration for which Pharaoh would go out. And that the people be gathered at noon, so that they may attend my command and your command. And from his saying: And that the people be gathered at noon, it is raised in conjunction with his saying: the day of adornment. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Nahik regarding this: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abdul-Mumin told us: I heard Abu Nahik say: And that the people will be gathered at noon, meaning Pharaoh will gather his people.
20:60: And His statement, So Pharaoh turned away, God Almighty says: So Pharaoh turned away, ignoring what he had brought of the truth. So he gathered his plot, meaning: he gathered his deceit, and that was his gathering of his magicians after he had taken them by learning them. Then he came, meaning: then everyone came to the appointment that Moses had promised him, and he came with his magicians.
20:61: God Almighty says: Moses said to the magicians when Pharaoh brought them Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against God meaning: Do not invent a lie against God, and do not say it for He will destroy you with a punishment so He will uproot you with destruction and wipe you out. The Arabs have two dialects for it: saht extortion and asaht destruction. Saht is more common than asaht destruction. It is said from it: saht al-dahr he extorted time, and asaht mal so-and-so: if he destroyed it, so he destroys it as saht extortion, and asahtah he destroys it, yashtah destruction, and ishatan destruction. Among the ishatan is the saying of al-Farazdaq: There was a time, O Ibn Marwan, when he did not leave any money except what was wiped out or wasted. It is narrated: Except if it is wiped or polished. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, He will destroy you with a punishment, meaning: He will destroy you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He will destroy you with a punishment. He said: He will uproot you with a punishment. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He will destroy you with a punishment, he said: He will uproot you with a punishment and destroy you. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He will destroy you with a punishment, he said: He will destroy you with a destruction in which there is no remainder. He said: And that which is destroyed has no remainder. Musa told us: Amr told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: He will destroy you with a punishment. He said: He will destroy you with a punishment. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it as fisahtkum with a fatha on the ya from saht yasaht. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as fisahtkum with a damma on the ya from asaht yasaht. Abu Ja`far said: The statement in this regard, according to us, is that they are two well-known readings, and two well-known languages with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. However, the fat-ha in it is more pleasing to me because it is the language of the people of Aliyah, and it is more eloquent, and the other, which is the damma, is in Najd. His saying, And he who fabricates will fail, means: And he who creates a lie and says it, by his lie, will not attain the need that he sought through it and hoped to attain through it.
20:62: God Almighty says: The magicians disputed among themselves about their affair. Their dispute over their affair among themselves was reported to have been that some of them said to others: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they disputed their affair among themselves and whispered secretly, the magicians said among themselves: If this is a magician, then we will defeat him, and if he is from the heaven, then he has a command. Others said: Rather, some of them said to each other: This is not the saying of a magician. Who said that? Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: I was told by Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Every magician gathered his ropes and staffs, and Moses went out with his brother leaning on his staff, until he reached the assembly, and Pharaoh was in his council, with him were the nobles of his kingdom, and the people had been entrusted to him. Then Moses said to the magicians when he came to them: Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against God, or He will destroy you with a punishment, and he who invents a lie has failed. So the magicians took turns among themselves, and some of them said to others: This is not the speech of a magician. And His saying, And they whispered secretly, God Almighty says: The magicians whispered secretly among themselves. Then the scholars differed about the secret they kept, and some of them said: It was what some of them said to each other: If this is a magician, then we will defeat him, and if it is from the command of heaven, then he will defeat us.
20:63: And others said about that, what: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: I was told by Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Some of them pointed to each other, whispering: These two are magicians who want to expel you from your land with their magic. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, And they disputed their affair among themselves and held secret talks without Moses and Aaron. They said in their secret talks: Indeed, these two are magicians who want to expel you from your land with their magic and do away with your best way. They said: Indeed, these two are magicians, meaning by their saying: Indeed, these two are Moses and Aaron, they are magicians who want to expel you from your land with their magic. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, these two are magicians who want to expel you from your land with their magic, referring to Moses and Aaron, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement, Indeed, these two are magicians. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it, Indeed, these two with emphasis on in and with the alif in hadhaan, and they said: We read it like that. Some of the Arabists from Basra used to say that in is light in meaning heavy, and it is a language of a people who raise it and insert the lam to differentiate it from what has the meaning of something. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: That is in two ways: One of them is according to the language of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka’b and those who live near them, they make the two in their raising, accusative, and genitive with the alif. A man from Asad recited to me on the authority of some of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka’b: He lowered his head like a brave man, and if he had seen a way for the brave man to attack him, he would have been deaf. He said: It was also narrated from him: This is my brother’s handwriting, I know it. He said: And that, even though it is little, is more correct, because the Arabs said: Muslims, so they made the waw follow the damma, because it is not declined, then they said: I saw the Muslims, so they made the ya follow the kasra of the meem. They said: So when they saw that the ya of the two could not be kasra what preceded it, and it remained open, they left the alif following it, so they said: Two men in every case. He said: The Arabs agreed to prove the alif in both men, in the nominative, accusative and genitive, and they are two, except for Banu Kinanah, for they say: I saw both men, and I passed both men, and it is ugly and little, and they followed the analogy. He said: The other way is to say: I found the alif of this a support, and it is not a lam of fa’la, so when it was built, you added a nun to it, then you left the alif fixed as it was and does not change in any case, as the Arabs said: alladhi, then they added a nun to indicate the plural, so they said: alladhi in their nominative, accusative, and genitive, just as they left these two in their nominative, accusative, and genitive. He said: The analogy was to say: al-dhun. Another of them said: That is from the jazm mursal, and if it was accusative, it would have gone out to the expansion. And he narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah Muammar bin Al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Amr, Isa bin Omar, and Yunus said: These two are magicians in pronunciation, and they wrote these two as they wanted the book, and the pronunciation is correct. He said: Abu Al-Khattab claimed that he heard some people from Banu Kinanah and others, raising the two in the place of the accusative and genitive. He said: Bishr bin Hilal said: Indeed means the beginning and affirmation. Do you not see that it works on what follows it, and does not work on what comes after it, so it raises the report and does not make it accusative, as it made the noun accusative, so the metaphor of Indeed these two are magicians was a metaphor of two statements, its point of articulation is: Indeed: Yes, then I said: These two are magicians. Do you not see that they raise the common like the saying of Dabi’: Whoever spends the night in the city, then I and Qiyar are strangers there And he said: The swords came and went, leaving Hawazin like the horns of a fierce fox. He said: Some of them say: God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet, so they raise it to the level of partnership in the beginning, and they do not work in it if. He said: I heard the eloquent ones among the people of ihram say: Indeed, all praise and blessings are Yours, and the kingdom, You have no partner. He said: And some people read it with a lightened nun in if and a sukun on it. He said: And it is permissible, because they have inserted the lam in the beginning, and it is a separation. He said: Umm Al-Halis for the old woman Shahraba He said: Some people claimed that it is not permissible, because if the nun of in is lightened, then it is necessary for him to include illa and say: Indeed, this is nothing but two magicians. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading in this regard according to us is in with a shaddah on the nun and hadhaan with an alif due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and that it is thus in the script of the Mushaf. Its reason, when read thus, is that it resembles alladhi when they add a nun to alladhi and the i’rab is maintained in all cases as one. Likewise, hadhaan with a nun added to hadha is maintained in all cases as one. This is the language of Harith ibn Ka`b, Khatham, Zubayd, and those tribes of Yemen who are their followers. And his saying, And they will go with your best way, meaning: and they will overcome your masters and nobles. It is said: He is the way of his people and the one looked up to by his people and their peer if he is their master and noble and the one looked up to. This is said for the singular and the plural, and they may have made it plural, so they said: These are the ways of their people, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: We were different ways (al-Jinn 72:11) and these are the peers of their people. As for his saying the like, it is the feminization of the like. It is said for the feminine: Take the like from them. And in the masculine: Take the like from them. The like is made singular, and it is an attribute and description of the group, as it is said: To Him belong the best names (Ta-Ha: 8-al-Hashr 59:24). It may be possible that the like is made feminine because of the feminization of the way. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying in your best way, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And they will go with your best way, meaning: your best, and they are the Children of Israel. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And they will go away with your best way, he said: Those of reason, honor, and lineage. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And they will go with your best way, he said: Those of intelligence, nobility, and lineage. Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Yazid told us: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And they will take away your best way, and their best way at that time was the Children of Israel, and they were the most numerous of the people in terms of wealth and children. The enemy of God said: They only want to take them away for themselves. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, in your best way, he said: in the Children of Israel. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And they will go with your best way, meaning: They will go with the nobles of your people. Others said: The meaning of this is: And they change your way and religion that you are following, from their saying: So-and-so has a good way. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and they will go away with your best way, he said: They will go away with what you are upon, they will change what you are upon. And he recited: “Leave me to kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption to appear on earth.” (Ghafir 40:26) He said: This is His statement, and they will go away with your best way, and he said: He says, your way today is a good way, so if you change it, this way will be gone. It was narrated on the authority of Ali regarding the meaning of his saying: And they go with your best way as follows: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: They turn people’s faces towards them. Abu Ja`far said: This statement that Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And they go with your best way, even if it is a statement that has a meaning that the speech can bear, the interpretation of the people of interpretation is contrary to it, so I do not permit that statement to be made.
20:64: The readers differed in their reading of his statement: So, gather your plot. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa read it as So, gather your plot with a hamza on the alif of So, gather. They directed the meaning of that to: So, perfect your plot and resolve to do it, from their saying: So-and-so gathered to go out, and gathered to go out, just as it is said: he resolved to do it. From this is the saying of the poet: I wonder, for hopes are of no avail, will I ever become one day when my affair is resolved? What he means by his saying: agreed upon is that he has decided and resolved to do it. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever does not resolve to fast from the night, then his fast is not valid. Some of the readers of Basra read it as gather your guidikum by connecting the alif and leaving out its hamza, from gathered something, as if he directed it to the meaning: Do not leave anything of your guidance without bringing it. And some of the readers of this reading used to find fault, as I was told, with his reading of it in this way, by saying: So Pharaoh turned away and gathered his guidance (Ta-Ha 20:6). Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading of this according to us is to pronounce the hamza on the alif of ajma`, because the proof of the reciters has agreed upon it, and that the magicians were those who were known for it, so there is no reason to say to them: Gather what you have been called upon for from what you know, because a person only gathers what he does not have with what he has, and that was not the day when their knowledge of what they were doing of magic increased, rather it was the day when it was revealed, or it was scattered from what he had, some of it to some, and the magic was not scattered with them so that they would gather it. As for his statement: So he gathered his plot (Ta-Ha 20:60), it is not similar in meaning to his statement: So gather your plot, because Pharaoh was the one who gathered and celebrated what he would defeat Moses with from what he did not have gathered and present, so it was said: So Pharaoh took over and gathered his plot. His saying: Then come in rows means: attend and come in rows. The row here is a source, and that is why it is singular. Its meaning is: then come in rows. The row in the speech of the Arabs has another place, which is the saying of the Arabs: I came to the row today, meaning the prayer place in which one prays. And his saying: And he who has been arrogant has succeeded today, meaning: he who has been arrogant to his companion and has defeated him has achieved his need today. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: I was told by Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Pharaoh gathered the people for that gathering, then he ordered the magicians and said: Come in rows, and today he who has gained the upper hand has succeeded. That is, today he who has overcome his companion has succeeded.
20:65: God Almighty says: So the magicians gathered their plot, then they came in a row and said to Moses: O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw. He left out mentioning that from the speech, being satisfied with the speech indicating it. There is a difference of opinion regarding the number of magicians who came in rows that day. Some of them said: They were seventy thousand magicians, with each magician carrying a rope and a stick. Who said that? Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza told us: Pharaoh gathered seventy thousand magicians, and they threw down seventy thousand ropes and seventy thousand sticks. Then Moses threw down his stick, and behold, it was a clear serpent, opening its mouth and swallowing their ropes and sticks. Then the magicians fell down in prostration at that point, and they did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell and the reward of their people. Then they said, We will not prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us. Others said: Rather, they were more than thirty thousand men. Who said that? Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: They said, ‘O Musa, either you throw or we will be the ones who throw.’ Musa said to them: Throw. So they threw their ropes and sticks, and they were thirty-two thousand men, and there was not a man among them who did not have a rope and a stick with him. Others said: Rather, they were fifteen thousand. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: I was told by Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: A row of fifteen thousand magicians, with each magician’s ropes and sticks. Others said: Rather, they were nine hundred. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: The magicians were three hundred from Al-Arish, and three hundred from Fayoum, and they doubted three hundred from Alexandria, so they said to Moses: Either you throw what you have before us, or we throw what we have before you, and that is his saying: Or we will be the first to throw, and that in his saying either is in the accusative case, and that is because the meaning of the speech is: Choose, O Moses, one of these two matters: Either you throw before us, or we will be the first to throw, and if someone said: It is a nominative, it would be a doctrine, as if he directed it to it being a predicate like the saying of the one who says: So go, either to fulfill a need or to find a good and friendly resting place.
20:66: And His statement: He said, 'Rather, throw' God Almighty says: Moses said to the magicians: Rather, you throw what you have before me. And His statement: Then, behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him, because of their magic, to be crawling, and in this statement there is an omission, which is: So they threw what they had of ropes and staffs, and behold, their ropes, he omitted mentioning it because the statement that was mentioned about it was sufficient. And He mentioned that the magicians bewitched the eyes of Moses and the eyes of the people before they threw their ropes and staffs, so it appeared to Moses then that they were crawling. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: I was told by Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: They said, O Moses, Either you throw or we will be the first to throw. He said, Rather, throw. So the first thing they took away with their magic was the sight of Moses and the sight of Pharaoh, then the sight of the people after that. Then each man threw what he had in his hand of sticks and ropes, and behold, they were serpents like ropes, filling the valley, some riding on others. The reading of the statement: It appears to me that it moves differed. The majority of the readers of the regions read it as It appears to me that it moves with a ya, meaning: It appears to them that it moves. If it is read in this way, then an is in the nominative case. It was narrated from Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read it takhal with a ta, meaning: He used to imagine their ropes and sticks that they move. If he used to read it in this way, then an is in the accusative case because takhal is connected to it. It was mentioned from some of them that he used to read it takhal to mean: You imagine it to you. If it is read in this way also, then an is in the accusative case meaning: You imagine it to be moving for them. The reading that I do not accept other than it is yakhil with a ya, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.
20:67: He, the Most High, means by His saying: So Moses felt fear within himself, but he found it.
20:68: And His saying: We said, ‘Do not fear, for you are the highest.’ God Almighty says: We said to Moses when he felt fear within himself, Do not fear, for you are the highest, over these magicians, and over Pharaoh and his army, and the one who conquered them.
20:69: And throw down what is in your right hand, it will swallow up what they have made. He says: And throw down your staff, it will swallow up their ropes and their staffs that they have used for magic, until it seems to you that they are moving. And his saying: They only made a magician’s trick. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as They only made a magician’s trick, raising the word keyed and with the alif in magician, meaning: What these magicians made was a magician’s trick. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as They only made a magician’s trick, raising the word keyed and without the alif in magic, meaning that what they made was a magician’s trick. In my opinion, they are two well-known readings with similar meanings. Kayd is deceit and trickery. The magician is deceived and his trick is from magic, and the deceit of magic and its deception is his imagining it to the bewitched, contrary to what it really is. The magician is a deceiver with magic, and magic is a deceiver with imagination. Whichever one you add kayd to is correct. It has been mentioned that some of them read kayd magic with the accusative of kayd. Whoever reads it in this way makes innama a single letter and works sana'u in kayd. Abu Jaafar said: This is a reading that I do not permit reading due to the consensus of the jurists among the reciters that it is not correct. His saying: And the magician will not succeed wherever he comes from means: And the magician will not achieve what he seeks with his magic, wherever he is. It has been mentioned from some of them that he used to say: The meaning of that is: The magician is killed wherever he is found. Some of the grammarians of Basra mentioned that this is in the letter of Ibn Masoud: And the magician will not succeed wherever he comes from. He said: The Arabs say: I came to you from where you do not know, and from where you do not know. And another of the Arabs said the first: The punishment for killing the magician wherever he comes from and wherever he comes from. He said: As for the saying of the Arabs: I came to you from where you do not know, and from where you do not know, it is only an answer that was not understood, so ask as they said: Where is the water and the grass.
20:70: And in this speech there is something omitted that has been dispensed with by the indication of what was omitted, which is: So Moses threw his staff, and it swallowed up what they had made. So the magicians fell down in prostration, saying, ‘We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.’ And it was mentioned that when Moses threw what was in his hand, it turned into a snake, and swallowed up everything that the magicians had thrown of ropes and sticks. Mentioning the narration of the one who said that: Ibn Humayd narrated: Yaqub narrated to us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: When they gathered and threw down what was in their hands of magic, “It appeared to him from their magic that it was crawling. So Moses felt fear within himself. We said, ‘Fear not; indeed, you are the superior. And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. ’” So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a clear serpent. He said: It opened its mouth like a pit, then placed its edge on the ground and raised the other, then it absorbed everything they had thrown of magic. Then he came to it and seized it, and behold, it was a staff. The magicians fell down in prostration. “They said, ‘We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses. ’ He said, ‘You have believed in him before I give you permission. Indeed, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides. ’” He said: The first to cut off hands and feet on opposite sides was Pharaoh. And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. He said: The first to be crucified on the trunks of palm trees was Pharaoh. Musa bin Harun told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, Then Moses felt fear within himself, so God revealed to him, Do not fear, “and throw down what is in your right hand,” it will swallow up what they are fabricating, “so he threw down his staff,” and every snake ate them, and when they saw that they prostrated themselves and said, ‘We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Aaron and Moses.’ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, saying: I was told by Wahb ibn Munabbih, So Moses felt fear in his soul when he saw what they had thrown of ropes and sticks and it seemed to him that they were crawling, and he said: By God, it was a stick in their hands, but it has turned into a snake, and this stick of mine does not crawl, or something like that. So God revealed to him: “Throw down what is in your right hand, it will swallow up what they have made. What they have made is only the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he goes.” Moses was happy and threw down his stick from his hand, and it looked at what they had thrown of their ropes and sticks, and they were snakes in the eyes of Pharaoh and the eyes of the people, crawling, so it began to swallow them, swallowing them snake by snake, until nothing could be seen in the valley, little or much of what they had thrown. Then Moses took it and it was a stick in his hand as it was, and the magicians fell down in prostration, saying: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses, if this had been magic it would not have defeated us.
20:71: And His saying: He said, ‘Did you believe in him before I gave you permission?’ God Almighty says: And Pharaoh said to the mockers: Did you believe and acknowledge Moses’ calling to what he had called you to before I gave you permission? He is your greatest one, he says: Moses is your greatest one who taught you magic. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, saying: I was told by Wahb ibn Munabbih, saying: When the magicians said: We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses, Pharaoh said to them, regretting and seeing the victory and the evidence: “You believed in him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic.” That is, he is the greatest magician who taught you. And His statement: Then I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides means: I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, between cutting that, which is to cut off the right hand and the left foot, or the left hand and the right foot, so that is cutting on opposite sides, and it was mentioned that the first to do that was Pharaoh, and we have mentioned the narration of that. And His statement: And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees means: I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, as the poet said: They crucified Al-Abdi on the trunk of a palm tree, and no old man sneezed except on his trunk. It means on a palm trunk. It was said: on trunks, because the one crucified on the wood is raised up its length, then he is placed on it, so it is said: he was crucified on it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, when the magicians saw what he had brought, they knew that it was from God, so they fell down in prostration, and believed at that. The enemy of God said: Then I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides... the verse. Musa bin Harun told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Pharaoh said: Then I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. So he killed them and cut them up, as Abdullah bin Abbas said when they said: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and let us die as Muslims (Al Imran 3:193). He said that they were magicians at the beginning of the day, and martyrs at the end of the day. And His saying: And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.
