Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, meaning: they will be humbled. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, meaning they will be humbled: they will submit to Me. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And the faces were humbled, he said: They were humbled. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, meaning faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: Faces will be humbled. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Talq said: When a man prostrates, his face is hidden from us, or he said: from us. Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Amr bin Marra, on the authority of Talq bin Habib, regarding this verse, And faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: It is the man lowering his head, his hands, and the tips of his feet. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Talq bin Habib, regarding his statement, And faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: It is placing your forehead, your hands, your knees, and the tips of your feet in prostration. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Talq bin Habib, regarding his statement, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: He placed the forehead and nose on the ground. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Talq bin Habib. Concerning His statement, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: It is prostration on the forehead, the palms of the hands, the knees, and the feet. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: Faces will be captive before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. They will all become captives to Him. He said: And the captive is the prisoner. We have explained the meaning of the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. And His statement, And he who carries injustice will fail, God Almighty says: He who carries to the place of resurrection associating partners with God, disbelieving in Him, and doing evil deeds against Him will not attain his need and his request. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And he who bears injustice will fail, he said: He who bears polytheism. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And he who bears injustice has failed, he said: He who bears polytheism. Injustice here means polytheism.
20:112: God Almighty says: And whoever does righteous deeds, which is what was said, performing the duties that God imposed on His servants, and he is a believer, meaning: he believes in God, and that He will reward those who obey Him and those who disobey Him for their disobedience, then he will fear no injustice, meaning: he will not fear that God will wrong him, by placing on him the sins of others, punishing him for them, nor deprivation, meaning: he will not fear that his good deeds will be deprived of him, thereby diminishing their reward. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, God only accepts from the deeds that are in faith. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, he said: They claimed that they are the obligatory duties. Mention of those who said what we said about the meaning of his saying, He does not fear injustice or oppression. Abu Kuraib and Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He does not fear injustice or oppression. He said: Oppression means usurpation. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me on the authority of Ali on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He does not fear injustice or oppression. He said: The son of Adam does not fear on the Day of Resurrection that he will be wronged, so his bad deeds will be added to him, nor will he be wronged, so his good deeds will be diminished. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will not fear injustice or deprivation, meaning: I will subdue you today, I will seize you with my strength and power, and I am able to subdue you and subdue you, for there is only justice between me and you, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, He will not fear injustice or oppression. As for oppression, it is that a man overpowers another man with his strength. God says on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:I will not take you by My strength and force, but justice is between Me and you, and there will be no injustice upon you. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement diminishment he said: diminishing something from the right of his work. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, who said: I heard Habib bin Abi Thabit say regarding His statement, nor diminishment. He said: Diminishment means diminishment. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So he will not fear injustice or deprivation, he said: Injustice is that his bad deeds will be increased, and his good deeds will not be diminished. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He does not fear injustice or deprivation, he said: He does not fear that he will be wronged, so he will not be rewarded for his work, and he does not fear that his right will be diminished, so he will not be given his work. Al-Harith told us: Al-Hasan told us: Salam bin Maskeen told us, on the authority of Maymun bin Siyah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God the Most High: So he will not fear injustice or deprivation, he said: God will not diminish anything from his good deeds, nor will He burden him with the sin of a wrongdoer. The root of digestion is: decrease. It is said: So-and-so deprived me of my right, and from this comes a woman who is thin, meaning one with a thin stomach, and from this comes their saying: The food has been digested, meaning it is gone. And I have diminished for you your right, meaning I have reduced you.
20:113: God Almighty says: Just as We have encouraged the people of faith to do good deeds, by promising them what We promised them, so We have warned the people of disbelief with threats against continuing to disobey Us and disbelieve in Our signs. So We sent down this Qur'an in Arabic, since they were Arabs. And We have diversified therein the threats. So We made them clear. He says: And We frightened them therein with various types of threats. Perhaps they will fear Us. He says: So that they will fear Us, by diversifying therein the threats. Or it will cause them to remember. He says: Or this Qur'an will cause them to take heed and learn from Our actions with the nations that denied the messengers before them, and they will be deterred from what they are doing, which is disbelief in God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’an, and We have diversified therein the warnings that they may fear what they were warned about of God’s command and punishment, and His events with the nations before them or that the Qur’an may cause them to remember: that is, seriousness and piety. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, or it causes them to remember, he said: Seriousness and piety. Some of them said about or it causes them to be remembered that its meaning is: or it causes them to be honored, through their belief in him.
20:114: God the Most High says: So He who is to be worshipped was raised from all His creation, the King whose authority overpowered every king and tyrant. The truth is above what the polytheists describe Him with from His creation: And do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you. God the Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not hasten, O Muhammad, with the Qur’an, so that you recite it to your companions, or recite it to them, before its meanings are revealed to you, so he was punished for writing it down and dictating what God had revealed to him from His Book, whoever used to write it down, before He explained its meanings to him. And it was said: Do not recite it to anyone, and do not dictate it to him, until We explain it to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not recite the Qur’an in haste before its revelation is completed to you, he said: Do not recite it to anyone until we make it clear to you. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: He says: Do not recite it to anyone until we complete it for you. This is what Al-Qasim said: until we complete it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you, means: Do not hasten until We make it clear to you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you: meaning its explanation. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you. He said: Its clarification. Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatada: Before His revelation is completed to you means before He makes His statement clear to you. And His saying, And say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge,’ God Almighty says: And say, O Muhammad: My Lord, increase me in knowledge in addition to what You have taught me. He commanded him to ask Him about the benefits of knowledge that he does not know.
20:115: God Almighty says: And if, O Muhammad, these people to whom We have directed the threat in this Qur’an should neglect My covenant, and disobey My command, and abandon My obedience, and follow the command of their enemy Satan, and obey him in opposition to My command, then their father Adam did that long ago, and We had already made a covenant with him, saying: And We had already enjoined upon Adam and said to him: This is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you from Paradise, but Satan whispered to him, so he obeyed him and disobeyed My command, and so My punishment befell him. And He, the Most High, meant by His saying, before, those to whom He informed that He had directed the threat in this Qur’an, and His saying, then he forgot, means: then he abandoned My covenant. As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, he said: So he abandoned it. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So he forgot, he said: He abandoned the command of his Lord. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found on his part no firm will, he said: He said to him, O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from Paradise and you become miserable, so he recited until he reached, Therein you will neither thirst nor be exposed to the sun, and he recited until he reached, And a kingdom that will not decay, he said: So he forgot what he had been made to do with that, he said: And this is God’s covenant with him, he said: And if he had had firm will, he would not have obeyed his enemy who envied him, and refused to prostrate to him with those to whom Satan prostrated, and disobeyed God who honored and glorified him, and commanded His angels to prostrate to him. Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed, Abd Al-Rahman, and Muammal told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He was called human because he was entrusted with something and he forgot. And his saying, And we found no determination on his part. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of determination here. Some of them said: Its meaning is patience. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And we found no determination in him, meaning patience. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatada: And we found no determination in him. He said: Patience. Ibrahim bin Yaqub al-Juwzjani told us: Abu al-Nadr told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: preservation. They said: Its meaning is: We did not find him preserving what we entrusted to him. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah: And we did not find in him determination. He said: Preserving what I commanded him. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Atiyah, regarding his statement, And We found no determination in him, he said: Preservation. Ibad bin Muhammad told us: Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Atiyah, regarding his statement, And we found no determination in him, he said: Preserving what I commanded him to do. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And we did not find in him determination, meaning: We did not find in him preservation. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And we found no determination in him, he said: Determination is preserving what God Almighty commanded him to preserve and adhering to it. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We found no determination in him, he said: We did not give him any determination. Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Al-Hajjaj bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Luqman bin Amir, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: If the dreams of the children of Adam were collected from the day God Almighty created Adam until the Day of Resurrection, and were placed on one side of a scale, and Adam’s dream was placed on the other side, his dream would be returned with their dreams, and God Almighty said: And We did not find on his part any determination. Abu Ja`far said: The root of determination is the heart’s belief in something. It is said: So-and-so resolved to do such-and-such if he believed in it and intended it. And from the belief of the heart is: preserving something, and from it is patience with something, because no one is impatient except one whose heart is weak and feeble. If that is the case, then there is no meaning more eloquent than what God Almighty has explained, which is His statement: And We found not in him determination. So its interpretation is: And We found not in him determination of heart, to fulfill his duty to God, nor to preserve what was entrusted to him.
20:116: God Almighty says, teaching His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Adam had not neglected his covenant, and that he knew that his children would not fail to follow his path, except for those whom God protected from among them. And remember, O Muhammad, When We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ and they prostrated, except for Iblis, who refused to prostrate to him.
20:117: So We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife.' That is why out of hatred for him he did not prostrate to you, and he disobeyed My command in that and disobeyed Me, so do not obey him in what he commands you to do, lest he expel you from Paradise because of your disobedience to your Lord and your obedience to him, and you become miserable. He says: So your livelihood will be from the toil of your own hands, so that is his misery that his Lord warned him of. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he used to plow with it, and he would wipe the sweat from its forehead. It was he about whom God Almighty said: So let him not expel you from Paradise, and you become miserable. So that was his misery. God Almighty said: So you become miserable, and He did not say: So you both become miserable. He said: So let him not expel you, because the beginning of the address from God was to Adam, peace be upon him. So in informing him of the punishment for his disobedience to Him, in what He forbade him from eating from the tree, it was sufficient to mention the woman, since it was known that her ruling in that was his ruling, as He said: On the right and on the left, seated. (Qaf: 17) It was sufficient for the listeners to know its meaning, from mentioning the action of its owner.
20:118: God Almighty says, informing about what He said to Adam when He settled him in Paradise: It is for you, O Adam, that you will neither go hungry nor naked therein. And in His statement that you will not go hungry therein is in the accusative case because of the that in His statement it is for you.
20:119: And his saying and that you will not be thirsty therein the readers differed in reading it, some of the readers of Medina and Kufa read it with a kasra, and you in apposition to his saying that you have. Some of the readers of Medina and most of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it with a fatha on its alif in apposition to the that in his saying that you will not be hungry therein. They directed the interpretation of that to that you have this and that, so this reading is the more pleasing of the two readings to me, because God, the Blessed and Most High, mentioned it, promised Adam that when He settled him in Paradise, so it is more appropriate for it to be in apposition to that you will not be hungry than it is the predicate of a subject, although the latter is not far from being correct. And what he meant by his saying you will not be thirsty therein is that you will not be thirsty in Paradise as long as you are in it, nor will you be exposed to the sun, he says: do not appear in the sun so that its heat will harm you, as Ibn Abi Rabi'ah said: She saw a man. If the sun is in the middle of the day, it will be lost. If the sun is in the middle of the day, it will be lost. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And you will neither thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun’s rays, meaning: You will neither be afflicted by thirst nor heat therein. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And you will neither thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun, meaning: you will not be afflicted by heat or harm. Ahmad bin Othman bin Hakim Al-Awdi told me: Abd Al-Rahman bin Sharik told us: My father told me, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: You will not be thirsty therein, nor will you be exposed to the sun. He said: The sun will not hit you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And do not be exposed to the sun. He said: Do not let the sun hit you.
20:120: , and his saying, Then Satan whispered to him, meaning: So Satan spoke to Adam and spoke to him, He said, ‘O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of immortality?’ He said: He said to him: Shall I direct you to a tree from which, if you eat from it, you will become immortal and will not die, and you will rule a kingdom that will not end or decay. As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, He said, ‘O Adam, shall I guide you to the tree of immortality and a kingdom that will not decay?’ If you eat from it, you will be a king like God, ‘or you will both be among the immortals.’ (al-A’raf 7:20) So you will never die.
20:121: God Almighty says: So Adam and Eve ate from the tree from which they were forbidden to eat, and they obeyed the command of Satan, and disobeyed the command of their Lord. So their private parts became apparent to them. He says: Their private parts were exposed to them, and they had been hidden from their eyes. As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: What he meant, meaning Satan, by his saying, Shall I guide you to the tree of immortality and a kingdom that will not decay, was to show them what was hidden from them of their private parts, by exposing their clothing. He had known that they had private parts because he had read from the books of the angels, but Adam did not know that, and their clothing was nails, so Adam refused to eat from it. So Eve came forward, ate, and then said: O Adam, eat, for I have already eaten, and it has not harmed me. So when Adam ate, their private parts became apparent to them. And his saying, And they began to fasten together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise, means: They began to fasten together from the leaves of Paradise. As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And they began to cover themselves with leaves of Paradise. He said: They began to cover themselves with fig leaves. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they began to fasten together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise, meaning: They connected over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And His statement, And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray, means: And he disobeyed the command of his Lord, and transgressed to what he should not have transgressed to, by eating from the tree from which He forbade him to eat. And His statement, He sinned, and his Lord chose him, then He accepted his repentance and guided him, means: His Lord chose him after his disobedience to Him, and granted him the provision to return to what pleases Him, and to work in obedience to Him, and that was his repentance for which He accepted his repentance. And His statement, and guided, means: And He guided him to repentance, so He granted him success in it.
20:122: Then his Lord chose him and accepted his repentance and guided him.
20:123: God Almighty says: God Almighty said to Adam and Eve, Descend from it, all of you, to the earth, some of you are enemies to one another. He says: You are the enemy of Satan and his offspring, and Satan is your enemy and the enemy of your offspring. And His statement, Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, meaning: If there comes to you, O Adam, Eve, and Iblis, guidance from Me? He says: An explanation of My path, and the religion that I have chosen for My creation. Then whoever follows My guidance, meaning: whoever follows My explanation and acts upon it, and does not deviate from it, will not go astray, meaning: he will not deviate from the path of truth, but he will be guided in this world and guided, nor will he be wretched in the Hereafter by the punishment of God, because God will admit him to Paradise and save him from His punishment. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Tahan told me: Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God guarantees that whoever recites the Qur’an and follows what is in it will not go astray in this world nor be miserable in the Hereafter. Then he recited this verse: So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be miserable. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me: Hakam Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Musa, on the authority of Marw, on the authority of Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: God has guaranteed. And he mentioned something similar. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Yasar Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told us: Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Nasa’i told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever recites the Qur’an and follows what is in it, God will protect him from misguidance and save him. I think he said: from the terror of the Day of Resurrection, because He said: So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer in the Hereafter.
20:124: God Almighty says, And whoever turns away from My remembrance with which I remind him, turning away from it and not accepting it or responding to it, and not taking heed from it so that he is deterred from what he is doing, which is his opposition to the command of his Lord, then he will have a depressed life meaning: then he will have a narrow life. And the narrow of homes, places and livelihoods means: severe. It is said: This is a narrow home: if it is narrow, and a difficult life. The male and female, the one and two and the plural with one pronunciation? And from it is the saying of Antarah: If they are in distress, then let them go. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then he will have a difficult life, meaning: misery. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement narrow he said: narrow. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then he will have a straitened life, he said: Strait means narrowness. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then he will have a straitened life, he said: narrow. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The people of interpretation differed about the place where God made for those who turned away from His remembrance the difficult life, and the state in which He placed them. Some of them said: He made that for them in the Hereafter in Hell, and that is because He made their food there the thorn and the zaqqum. Who said that? Muhammad bin Omar and bin Ali bin Muqaddam told me: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Then he will have a miserable life, he said: In Hell. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and he recited until he reached, and does not believe in the signs of his Lord, he said: These are the people of disbelief. He said: And a depressed life in the Fire, thorns of fire, and Zaqqum and Ghaslin. Adh-Dari’ is thorns of fire. There is no livelihood in the grave or in this world. Life and livelihood are only in the Hereafter. He recited the statement of God Almighty, Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life (al-Fajr 89:24). He said: For my livelihood. He said: And Ghaslin and Zaqqum are something that the people of this world do not know. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, For he will have a straitened life. He said: In the Fire. Others said: Rather, he meant by that: He has a life in this world that is forbidden. He said: God Almighty described their life as difficult, because even if what is forbidden is abundant, it is difficult. Who said that? Muhammad bin Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, a difficult life, he said: It is the life that God has made abundant for him from what is forbidden. Dawud bin Sulayman bin Yazid al-Maktab from the people of Basra told me: Amr bin Jarir al-Bajali told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, regarding God’s statement, a straitened life, he said: Provision in disobeying Him. Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me, he said: Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, he said: Abu Bastam told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, For he will have a straitened life, he said: filthy earnings. Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Sarari told me: Muhammad bin Suwar told us: Abu Al-Yaqzan Ammar bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Harun bin Muhammad Al-Taimi, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Then he will have a miserable life, he said: Evil work and bad sustenance. Others, who spoke about me, said that these people have a difficult life in this world. It is called difficult even though it is spacious, because they spend what they spend of their money in denial of God’s success, despair of God’s grace, and have bad thoughts about their Lord. Therefore, their life becomes difficult and narrow for them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life. He says: Every wealth that I give to one of My servants, whether little or much, who does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and it is the depression in life. It is said: A people who went astray turned away from the truth and were people of plenty in this world, so their life was difficult, and that is because they thought that God, the Almighty, would not spare them their livelihoods because of their bad opinion of God and their denial of Him. So if the servant denies God and has bad opinions of Him, his life will be difficult for him, and that is the depression. Others said: Rather, he meant by that: That is for them in the Barzakh, which is the torment of the grave. Who said that? Yazid bin Mukhallad Al-Wasiti told me: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said regarding God’s statement, a straitened life, he said: the torment of the grave. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us: Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of al-Nu’man bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: The difficult life, which God said is the torment of the grave. Hawthara bin Muhammad Al-Manqari told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri: For he will have a narrow life. He said: His grave will be so narrow that his ribs will overlap. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: My father and Shuaib ibn al-Layth told us, on the authority of al-Layth: Khalid ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abi Saeed, that he used to say: A difficult life is the torment of the grave. Ninety-nine dragons are set upon the unbeliever in his grave, biting him and scratching his flesh until he is resurrected. And it was said: If one of these dragons were to blow on the earth, no crops would grow. Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Muhammad bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The grave of the unbeliever will close over him until his ribs interlock in it, and this is the difficult life of which God said: A difficult life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. Abu Kuraib told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh and Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: A difficult life, he said: The torment of the grave. Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement: Then he will have a depressed life, he said: The torment of the grave. Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad told me, he said: Muhammad bin Rabi’ah told us, he said: Abu Umays told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mukhariq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his statement: A difficult life, he said: The torment of the grave. Abdul Rahim Al-Barqi told me, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Jaafar and Ibn Abi Hazim told us, they said: Abu Hazim told us, on the authority of Al-Nu’man Ibn Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, A difficult life, he said: The torment of the grave. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: It is the torment of the grave which: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, on the authority of Daraj, on the authority of Ibn Hujaira, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do you know why this verse was revealed: For him is a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. Do you know what a depressed life is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: The punishment of the disbeliever in his grave. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, ninety-nine dragons will be set upon him. Do you know what a dragon is? Ninety-nine snakes, each with seven heads. They blow into his body, sting him, and scratch him until the Day of Resurrection. And God, the Blessed and Most High, followed that with His saying: And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting. So it was known from that that the difficult life that God made for them is before the punishment of the Hereafter, because if that were in the Hereafter, then His saying: And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting would not have an understood meaning, because if that were not preceded by a punishment for them before the Hereafter, so that what is in the Hereafter would be more severe than it, then the meaning of His saying: And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting would be invalidated. So since that is the case, then that difficult life that God made for them is not without being for them in their worldly life, or in their graves before the resurrection, since there is no reason for it to be in the Hereafter for what we have explained. If it is for them in their worldly life, then it must be that everyone who turns away from the remembrance of God from the disbelievers, then his life in it is difficult, and in our existence many of them have a more spacious life than many of those who turn to the remembrance of God, the Blessed and Most High, who say to Him the believers in that, which indicates that that is not the case. And since the statement in that is free of these two aspects, the third aspect is correct, which is that it is in The isthmus. And His statement: And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the blindness that God mentioned in this verse, that he will be resurrected as the one who will destroy the infidels on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: That is blindness to the argument, not blindness to sight. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement: And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind, he said: He has no argument. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind, he said: on the authority of Al-Hujjah. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And it was said: He will be resurrected blind of sight. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement about that is what God Almighty said, which is that he will be resurrected blind to the argument and seeing things, as He, may His praise be glorified, informed us, so He was general and did not specify.
20:125: And his saying: “He said: My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was seeing?” The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said about that, what: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: “He said: ‘My Lord, why have You raised me blind?’ I have no argument.” And his saying: And I was seeing. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And I was seeing my proof. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And I was seeing, he said: Knowing of my proof. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: I had insight with which I could see things. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And I was seeing in this world. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “He said: My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I used to be seeing?” He said: He was far-sighted, short-sighted, blind to the truth. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is that God, the Mighty and Sublime, has made the report about Himself comprehensive by describing Himself with sight, and has not singled out one meaning from Him over another, so that is according to what He has made comprehensive. So since that is the case, then the interpretation of the verse is: My Lord, why have You raised me blind to my proof and to seeing things, when I was in this world with sight of all of that? If someone were to say: How could this man say to his Lord: Why have You raised me blind? while witnessing His great power? Was he ignorant in that situation that God could do with him whatever He wished, or what was the reason for that? It would be said: That was a question from him to his Lord to inform Him of the crime for which he deserved that, since he was ignorant of it and thought that he had no crime for which he deserved that from Him, so he said: Lord, for what sin and for what crime have You raised me blind, when I was previously sighted in this world, and You do not punish anyone except without what he deserves from You in terms of punishment.
20:126: And His statement: "He said: Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them." God Almighty says: God said then to the one who said to Him: Why did You raise me blind while I was seeing? I did that to you, so I raised you blind just as My signs came to you, which are His proofs, evidence, and explanation that He explained in His Book, and you forgot them? He says: So you abandoned them and turned away from them. And you did not believe in them, and did not act. And what He meant by His statement: Thus did it come to you is this is how it came to you. And His statement: And thus today you will be forgotten means: Just as you forgot Our signs in the world, and abandoned them and turned away from them, so today We will forget you, and leave you in the Fire. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement: And thus today you will be forgotten. Some of them said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement: And thus today you will be forgotten, he said: In the Fire. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them, he said: So you left them. And thus today you are forgotten, and thus today you are left in the Fire. It was narrated on the authority of Qatada regarding this matter: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “He said: Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them. And thus is this Day you are forgotten.” He said: He forgot the good, but he did not forget the evil. This statement that Qatada said is close in meaning to what Abu Salih and Mujahid said, because leaving them in the Fire is the greatest evil for them.
20:127: God Almighty says: And thus do We recompense: that is, We reward those who transgress and disobey their Lord, and do not believe in His Messengers and Books, so We make for them a difficult life in the intermediate realm, as we have explained before. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting. God Almighty says: And the punishment in the Hereafter is more severe for them than what I promised them in the grave of a difficult life and more lasting. He says: And more lasting than it, because it is without time or end.
20:128: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have your people not been guided who associate others with God? The meaning of guide is make clear. He says: “Have they not been made clear how many nations We destroyed before them, who followed the path before them, who walk in their dwellings and homes, and who see the effects of Our punishments that We have brought upon them, the evil consequences of what they are continuing in of disbelief in Our verses, and who are admonished by them, and take heed, and turn to submission, and believe in God and His Messenger, for fear that what happened to them will happen to them because of their disbelief in God.” And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: How many generations before them have We destroyed who walked in their dwellings because Quraysh used to trade to Ash-Sham, and pass by the dwellings of Aad and Thamud and those like them, and they would see the traces of the events of God’s decrees upon them, so He said to them: “So they were not warned by what they saw of Our action upon them because of their disbelief in Us, that something similar would descend upon them, while they are continuing in the same manner as they did.” Al-Farra’ used to say: It is not permissible for how many in this place to be anything other than the accusative of we destroyed, and he used to say: And even if it is only the accusative, the entire statement is raised by His statement: it guides them, and he said: That is like the statement of the one who says: It has become clear to me whether Amr or Zaid stayed in the question, and like His statement: It is the same for you whether you call upon them or whether you are silent (al-A’raf 7:193), and he claims that there is something in it that raises whether that does not appear with the question, he said: If you had said: It is the same for you whether you are silent or calling upon them, that raising in the sentence would have become clear. And what Al-Farra’ said is not like that, as he said: Because even though kam is one of the interrogative letters, it was not used in this position for interrogation, rather it is in the position of the described nouns. And the meaning of the statement is what we mentioned before, which is: Have not the generations before them who walk in their dwellings made clear to them the great number of Our destructions, or have not the perishing generations guided them? It has been mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah, Have not those We destroyed guided them? So kam is in the position of min in the reading of Abdullah, it is in the nominative case with his saying: He guides them. This is the most apparent of its aspects and the most correct of its meanings, even though what he said has a distant aspect and approach. And His statement: Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding. God Almighty says: Indeed in what these people witness and see of the effects of Our events with the nations that denied Our messengers before them, and Our examples of them for their disbelief in God, are signs. He says: evidence, lessons, and sermons. For those of understanding. That is, for the people of wisdom and intellect, and whoever his intellect, understanding, and religion prevent him from doing what harms him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: For those of understanding means: those who are pious. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding the people of piety.
20:129: God Almighty says: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord O Muhammad, whoever has a term decreed for him, he will not exceed it before he reaches his term. And a specified term means: And a specified time with your Lord that He has named for them in the Mother of the Book and written in it, they will reach it and complete it. It would have been inevitable means: Destruction would have been inevitable for them immediately. It is a source from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so is constant with so-and-so, he is constant with him, constant and inevitable: if he does not leave him. He presented his saying it would have been inevitable before his saying: A specified term. The meaning of the statement is: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been inevitable, so be patient with what they say. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been an obligation and a specified term. The specified term is the world. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable and a specified term. This is one of the introductions to speech. He says: Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord to a specified term, it would have been inevitable, and the specified term is the Hour, because God Almighty says: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter. (al-Qamar 54:46) Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding and a specified term, he said: This is brought forward and postponed, and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been binding. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his saying: It would have been binding. Some of them said: Its meaning is: It would have been death. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told me: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: It would have been binding means: death. Others said: It means it would have been murder. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: It would have been binding. Binding means killing.
20:130: And His saying: So be patient over what they say God the Most High says to His Prophet: So be patient, O Muhammad, over what these deniers of God's signs from your people say to you: You are a magician, you are a madman, a poet, and similar sayings. And glorify the praises of your Lord He says: Continue with your praise of your Lord. And He said: With the praise of your Lord, and the meaning is: With your praise, your Lord, just as you say: I liked Zaid's hitting, and the meaning is: My hitting Zaid. And His saying: Before sunrise and that is the dawn prayer and before its sunset which is the afternoon prayer and during the hours of the night which are the hours of the night, the singular of which is: I, on the assumption of a load, and from this is the saying of Al-Munakhal Al-Saadi: Sweet and bitter, like the affection of the cup, its bitterness is in every one of my thoughts, I spend the night wearing shoes What he means by his saying: And during the hours of the night glorify God is the last evening prayer, because it is performed after some hours of the night have passed. His saying: And the ends of the day: meaning the Dhuhr and Maghrib prayers. It was also said: the ends of the day. What is meant by that are the two prayers that we mentioned, because the Dhuhr prayer is at the end of the first end of the day, and at the beginning of the end of the other day, so it is at two ends of it, and the third end is sunset, and at that time the Maghrib prayer is performed, so that is why it was said: ends. It may also be possible to say: what is meant by it are the two ends of the day. It was also said: ends, as it was said: Your hearts have become hardened (al-Tahrim 66:4), so it was pluralized, and what is meant is: two hearts, so that is the first end of the other day, and the last end of its first end. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Zayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. He said: The obligatory prayer. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, saying: Ismail bin Abi Khalid informed us, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Jarir bin Abdullah, who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he saw the moon on the night of the full moon and said: You will see your Lord as you see this, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in praying before sunrise and before sunset, then do so. Then he recited: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. Ibn Jurayj said: The afternoon and the ends of the day. He said: The obligatory prayer. Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun, he said: It is the dawn prayer. And before its setting, he said: The afternoon prayer. And during the hours of the night, he said: The sunset and evening prayers. And at the ends of the day, he said: The noon prayer. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And during the hours of the night, glorify [God] and at the ends of the day: He said: During the hours of al-Layl 92:darkness. And at the ends of the day: sunset and dawn. And His statement and at the ends of the day is in the accusative case in apposition to His statement: before the rising of the sun, because the meaning of that is: So glorify the praises of your Lord at the end of the night and at the ends of the day. And similar to what we said about the meaning of night watches, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: And during the hours of the night he said: The place of prayer throughout the night. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Al-Hasan, And during the hours of the night he said: From its beginning, its middle, and its end. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And during the hours of the night glorify God, he said: The hours of al-Layl 92:the middle of the night. And his saying: Perhaps you will be satisfied means: so that you will be satisfied. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Iraq recited it as perhaps you will be satisfied with the ta’ open. Asim and al-Kisa’i recited it as perhaps you will be satisfied with the ta’ closed. This was narrated from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami. It seems that those who recited it with the fat-ha had the meaning: God gives you, until you are satisfied with His gift and reward for you. This is how the people of interpretation interpreted it. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Perhaps you will be satisfied, he said: The reward, you will be satisfied with what God will reward you for. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Perhaps you will be satisfied, he said: with what you are given. And those who read it with the dammah directed the meaning of the speech to perhaps God will satisfy you with your worship of Him and your obedience to Him. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings, each of which has been recited by scholars among the reciters. They are two readings that are widespread in the recitation of the regions, and they agree in meaning, not differing in it. This is because if God Almighty, may He be exalted, pleases him, then there is no doubt that he is pleased, and if he is pleased, then God has pleased him. So each of them indicates the meaning of the other, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.
20:131: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And do not look at what We have made for those like them who turn away from the signs of their Lord and their likes, a pleasure in their worldly life, which they enjoy, of the flower of the immediate world and its freshness, to test them thereby meaning: to test them in what We have given them of that, and to try them, for that is fleeting and transient, and a deception and trick that will vanish. And the provision of your Lord which He promised you that He will provide for you in the Hereafter until you are satisfied, and it is His reward for it, is better for you than what We have given them of the flower of worldly life. And more lasting meaning: more lasting, because it is unending and never ending. He mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, because the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent to a Jew to borrow food from him, but he refused to lend him anything except a pledge. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to a Jew to ask him for a loan, but he refused to give him anything except a pledge. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became sad, so God revealed: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, the splendor of the life of this world. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Muhammad ibn Katheer narrated: Abdullah ibn Waqid narrated: Yaqub ibn Yazid narrated: Abu Rafi’ said: A guest visited the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), so he sent me to a Jew in Medina to ask him for a loan. I came to him and he said: I will not lend him a loan except with a pledge. I informed him of that, and he said: I am trustworthy among the people of heaven and earth, so carry my shield to him. Then this verse was revealed: And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an (al-Hijr 15:87). And His statement: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, the splendor of the life of this world until His statement: And the [best] outcome is for righteousness. By His statement: categories of them He means men of different kinds, and by the splendor of the life of this world: the adornment of the life of this world. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: The flower of the life of this world means the adornment of the life of this world. The flower of the life of this world is in the accusative case because of the exit from the ha’ in his saying with it from We enjoyed it just as it is said: I passed by the noble and generous one, so the noble and generous one is in the accusative case based on the verb I passed by. And likewise his saying: To that by which We have given enjoyment to some of them, the flower of the life of this world is in the accusative case based on the verb meaning: We gave them enjoyment with it, a flower in the life of this world and an adornment for them in it. Al-Farra’ mentioned that some of the Banu Faq’as recited to him: The one who is at the foot of the foothills is a hostage of planets, buried in dust and rocks. So, the verb raheena is placed in the accusative case as a preposition from his saying: He removed the one at the foothills. This is undoubtedly weaker in its action as an accusative than his saying: We gave enjoyment to some of their spouses with it, because the agent in the noun, which is raheena, is a prepositional letter, not an accusative. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: To test them therein means: To test them therein. And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting than what these people have given us of this world.
20:132: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And enjoin O Muhammad prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it meaning: be steadfast in performing it and performing it within its limits. We do not ask you for provision meaning: We do not ask you for money, rather We charge you with physical work, for which We will give you a great reward and abundant recompense. We provide for you meaning: We give you the money and earn it for you, and We do not ask you for it. And His statement: And the good outcome is for the righteous meaning: and the good outcome of every action is for the people of piety and fear of God, not for those who do not fear punishment for themselves or hope for reward for themselves. And similar to what we said about His statement: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, who said: Whenever Urwah saw what the rulers had, he would enter his house and say: “Do not strain your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them - the splendor of worldly life - by which We test them. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the [best] outcome is for righteousness.” Then he would call out: “Prayer, prayer. May God have mercy on you.” Abu Kuraib told us: Othman told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, that whenever he saw something of this world, he would go to his family and say: Prayer. “And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision.” Al-Abbas bin Abdul-Azim told us: Jaafar bin Awn told us: Hisham bin Saad told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: One of Umar bin Al-Khattab’s servants, Yarfa and I, would spend the night with him. He had an hour of the night in which he would pray. When we said that he would not get up at night, he would stand up. When he prayed at night and then finished, he would recite this verse: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant in it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Hisham bin Saad told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, the same.
20:133: God Almighty says: These polytheists, whose characteristics He described in the verses before, said: Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from his Lord, just as Salih brought his people with the she-camel and Jesus brought the dead back to life and healed the blind and the leper? God Almighty says: Did there not come to them the explanation of what was in the books before this book of the report of the nations before them whom We destroyed when they asked for signs and disbelieved in them when they came to them, how We hastened the punishment for them and sent down Our punishment because of their disbelief in them? He says: So what will assure them, if the sign comes to them, that their condition will not be like the condition of those people? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: Did there not come to them a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures? He said: The Torah and the Gospel. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Did there not come to them a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures? The scriptures that were emptied of the nations in whose dwellings they walk.
20:134: God Almighty says: And if We had destroyed these polytheists who deny this Qur’an before We sent it down to them, and before We sent a caller calling them to what We imposed upon them in it, with a punishment We would have inflicted upon them for their disbelief in God, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection when they came to Us and We intended to punish them: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a Messenger calling us to Your obedience, so that we would follow Your signs? He says: So that we would follow Your proof and evidence and what You sent down to him of Your commands and prohibitions before We were humiliated by Your punishment and disgraced by it. Al-Fadl ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Qutaybah Sallam ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Three will argue with God on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the one who perished during the interval, the one whose mind was overcome, and the young boy. The one who perished during the interval will say: You did not give me a mind that I could benefit from. The one who perished during the interval will say: No messenger or prophet came to me, and if a messenger or prophet had come to me, I would have been the most obedient of Your creation to you. And he recited: Why did You not send us a messenger? The young boy will say: I was young and did not understand. He said: Then a fire will be raised for them and it will be said to them: Return it. He said: The one who, in God’s knowledge, was happy will return it, and the one who, in God’s knowledge, was weak will hesitate to do so, and He will say: You disobeyed Me, so how would My messengers be if they came to you?
20:135: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, are all of you polytheists waiting? He says: Waiting for who will be the successful one, and to what end my affair and your affair will be, waiting for the circles of time, so wait? He says: So watch and wait, for you will know who are the people of the straight and balanced path, in which there is no crookedness, when God's command comes and the Day of Resurrection comes, are we or you? And who is guided? He says: And you will know then who is the guided one who is on the path of the straight path, the one who is deliberate and does not deviate from his intention, from us and from you. In the word min from His statement: Then you will know who are the companions of the straight path, and the second from His statement: And who is guided, there are two aspects: the nominative, and the omission of the application of you know in them, as the Most High said: That We may know which of the two parties has the best count (al-Kahf 18:12), and the accusative is based on the application of you know in them, as the Most High said: And God knows the corrupter from the reformer (al-Baqarah 2:23).
